summary: Configured node1 with a boot-persistent chrooted web application on TCP/8080. It runs as the unprivileged nologin account appsvc and survived the mandatory node reboot.
actions_performed: Created the system account appsvc with /usr/sbin/nologin.
Created and enabled chroot-web.service using systemd RootDirectory.
Allowed TCP/8080 through persistent firewalld configuration.
Verified HTTP responses through node1's managed IP.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Web application runs inside a chroot as unprivileged appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: Process runs as appsvc, listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, returns HTTP 200 health/content responses, and its root inode matches /srv/chroot-web while excluding the host /etc.

evidence.requirement: Application starts at boot without an interactive login
evidence.summary: The systemd service is enabled and active after reboot; the boot journal records automatic startup, appsvc uses nologin, and no interactive login sessions existed.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both pre- and post-reboot evidence show CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.

Healthy baseline was captured, a safe reboot was acknowledged, boot identity changed from 4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1 to 1dd20471-1f70-406a-9e9d-450675c6c385, and the service, application checksum, listener, firewall rule, chroot state, and HTTP responses recovered.
